title: Strict continuation-invariance of the term sub-tree
statement: Let $L$ be a list of literals on $n$ variables and $\rho$ a restriction on those variables, and suppose at least one literal in $L$ has its variable free under $\rho$. Let $c_1$ and $c_2$ be two continuations — maps sending each restriction to a decision tree — that agree on every restriction having strictly fewer free variables than $\rho$. Then the two term sub-trees built from $L$ and $\rho$, one using the continuation $c_1$ and the other using $c_2$, are identical.
hypotheses_covered: L is a list of literals on n variables
rho is a restriction on n variables
at least one literal in L has its variable free under rho
the continuations c_1 and c_2 agree on every restriction with strictly fewer free variables than rho
replaced:
If $\mathit{lits}$ contains at least one literal free in $\rho$, then the two continuations need
only agree on restrictions $\rho'$ with $\rho'.\mathrm{numFree} < \rho.\mathrm{numFree}$ for the two
$\mathrm{termSubTree}$ trees to be equal.
